ASPECT aerial data collection supports the EPA Regional Superfund Programs during emergency responses, removal actions, and emergency preparedness activities. The ASPECT system has a mandate to provide emergency response services to a wide range of chemical/radiological emergency situations including actual or threatened releases, Special Event Assessment Rating (SEAR) events and Nationally Significant Security Events (NSSE). Consequently, it must be maintained at the highest operational readiness standard and must apply the highest quality, scientifically vetted detection and data processing algorithms. The ASPECT DPDS DOTO provides mission critical services ongoing maintenance of the ASPECT sensors, data processing and analysis, including: routine/scheduled maintenance, emergency repairs/maintenance, and system testing/evaluation; and specialized spectroscopy expertise, including hardware/software algorithm development, geospatial software development support, software integration, detection algorithm development, advanced infrared and radiological detection system development, advanced research and development, hardware and software system operation and maintenance, and aerial photographic/imaging systems integration support. 3 Contractor support is required due to the highly specific subject matter expertise required for sensor system operations, maintenance, and data analysis not currently available within the Agency. The Administration Building requires replacement of its 2,000-square-foot metal roof with a new asphalt shingle system that includes underlayment, drip-edge flashing, rotten fascia and sheathing repairs, and full gutter and downspout replacement. The existing metal system is not suited for the damp coastal environment and has resulted in deteriorated underlayment and recurring water intrusion at the ridges. Both projects will eliminate ongoing patch repairs, resolve code-compliance issues, and protect critical infrastructure housed within each facility. Work will be coordinated with the park’s project manager but performed primarily by the roofing contractor. Work Included Work under this contract includes complete removal and disposal of all existing roofing materials down to the roof deck for both buildings. The contractor will install new code-approved underlayment, full perimeter drip-edge flashing, and high-quality asphalt roofing systems with all required trim, fasteners, tie-downs, and manufacturer-specified components. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

SAINT LUCIA

UNLEASHING THE BLUE ECONOMY IN THE CARIBBEAN (UBEC)

IDA Credit # P171833

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services - Upgrade of the Leachate

 System

 

Reference No. LC-MOFED-541022-CS-CQS-ULS-26

 

Saint Lucia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to hiring a consulting firm to conduct a technical assessment and upgrade plan for the Deglos Leachate

 System.

 

The overall objective of this consultancy is to undertake the following tasks:

 

  • Technical Assessment of Existing Infrastructure
  • Environmental Compliance and Risk Evaluation
  • Assessment of the Operational Efficiency and Sus

System.

 

The overall objective of this consultancy is to undertake the following tasks:

 

  • Technical Assessment of Existing Infrastructure
  • Environmental Compliance and Risk Evaluation
  • Assessment of the Operational Efficiency and Sustainability of the Existing System
  • Upgrade Planning and Design
  • Prioritization and Implementation Roadmap
  • Decision-Support for Strategic Management

 

The engagement is expected to be completed within five (5) months, inclusive of the submission of deliverables to the client.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.finance.gov.lc

 

The Department of Finance now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

Firms wishing to signify their interest in undertaking the prescribed services are to submit an Expression of Interest providing information demonstrating that they have the required qualific

est in undertaking the prescribed services are to submit an Expression of Interest providing information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The information submitted should follow the layout indicated below:

 

1.         Background Information including Articles of Incorporation

2.         Information on the Firm’s qualifications, experience and competence relevant to the assignment (description of similar assignments undertaken including dates undertaken and reference information of clients).

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations: World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers November 2020 (“Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s   Procurement Regulations: World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers November 2020

award_criteria.text: TES. Description of Work: This Presolicitation notice announces an upcoming requirement for two cedar shingle roof replacements at the Gold Beach Ranger Station, located within the Gold Beach Ranger District in Curry County, Oregon. The existing cedar shingle roofs will be removed and replaced with new cedar shingles. The Gold Beach Ranger Station, located at 29279 Ellensburg Avenue in Gold Beach, Oregon, is situated along Highway 101 within one mile of the Pacific Ocean. The site and its buildings are considered to possess historical significance. The forthcoming solicitation will detail the selection process and outline all evaluation criteria that interested offerors will be required to address. One Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) contract is anticipated to be awarded. The estimated period of performance is 90 days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed, with work expected to begin in September 2026. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $100,000 and $150,000. Communications - Emphasis will be placed on instilling awareness among program participants concerning the use of communication devices. Aspects of Communications Security (e.g., e-mails, data fax & cellular phones) will be included in the awareness briefings. 4) Subcontractor Flow-down of OPSEC - All subcontractors’ Statement of Work will be reviewed by the OPSEC Coordinator prior to award of contractual work to determine OPSEC applicability. 5) Visitor Control - All visitors are required to process through established checkpoints for verification of identity, citizenship, personnel security clearances, appropriate certification of purpose of visit, issuance of badges, inspection of articles being brought into and out of the facilities and other such measures to assure proper visitor control. Escort for visitors shall be advised of proper escort procedures, limitation on disclosure, and other applicable controls involved in the visit. Program personnel shall be reminded through OPSEC briefings of the potential for the inadvertent release of information by visual and aural means when visitors are present. Activities of visitors and non-assigned personnel in the program areas shall be observed to determine that their presence is required by business needs an

rough an approved DOD on-line training package. 8.4. OPSEC AWARENESS CUI CUI 16 At least once quarterly, promote OPSEC awareness by publishing OPSEC bulletins, displaying OPSEC posters, disseminating OPSEC information or reminders via electronic communications (e-mail, marquees, etc.), or conducting in-person interviews with personnel. Coordinators and supervisors should make on-the-spot corrections of poor OPSEC practices and continuously use good OPSEC practices which will stress the important of OPSEC to mission success. 8.5. TRAINING OF DESIGNATED OPSEC OFFICIALS The OPSEC Coordinator will complete OPSEC Level II certification training by attending the Headquarters Department of the Army (HQDA) OPSEC Officers Course or a Service equivalent Operations Security Program (NOP) course. Additionally, it is recommended the OPSEC Coordinator receive external official presence (EOP) training. 8.6. award_criteria.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1_-_Statement_of_Objectives.pdf ===== CUI CUI STATEMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) 48th Maintenance Group F-35 Aircraft Wrap Around Stand 07 July 2026 1.0 Purpose The purpose of this requirement is to develop and obtain one (1) F-35A aircraft wrap-around phase stand to replace out-of-date and insufficient stands currently in use. 2.0 Background The 48th Equipment Maintenance Squadron (EMS) requires a complete, high- quality F-35A wrap-around maintenance platform to facilitate safe, effective, and efficient maintenance, repair, and inspection activities. The current existing stands are insufficient, creating safety hazards and wasting vital turnaround time when performing PHASE-level inspections on aircraft. 3.0 Scope The Contractor shall furnish all tools, vehicles, qualified personnel, materials, equipment, and services necessary to design, manufacture, test, deliver, assemble, and provide technical documentation for one (1) F-35A aircraft wrap-around stand. The stand must fully wrap around the aircraft to support maintenance operations while maximizing available hangar space and turnaround efficiency. 4.0 Period and Place of Performance Timeline: Within 24 weeks from the time of award (accommodating a minimum 120-day ARO lead time), the completed stand shall be delivered to RAF Lakenheath, assembled, and set up. Location: Installation and on-site assembly are to be performed at Building 1219 of RAF Lakenheath (RAFL), United Kingdom, IP27 9PN. ASPECT aerial data collection supports the EPA Regional Superfund Programs during emergency responses, removal actions, and emergency preparedness activities. The ASPECT system has a mandate to provide emergency response services to a wide range of chemical/radiological emergency situations including actual or threatened releases, Special Event Assessment Rating (SEAR) events and Nationally Significant Security Events (NSSE). Consequently, it must be maintained at the highest operational readiness standard and must apply the highest quality, scientifically vetted detection and data processing algorithms. The ASPECT DPDS DOTO provides mission critical services ongoing maintenance of the ASPECT sensors, data processing and analysis, including: routine/scheduled maintenance, emergency repairs/maintenance, and system testing/evaluation; and specialized spectroscopy expertise, including hardware/software algorithm development, geospatial software development support, software integration, detection algorithm development, advanced infrared and radiological detection system development, advanced research and development, hardware and software system operation and maintenance, and aerial photographic/imaging systems integration support. 3 Contractor support is required due to the highly specific subject matter expertise required for sensor system operations, maintenance, and data analysis not currently available within the Agency. The Administration Building requires replacement of its 2,000-square-foot metal roof with a new asphalt shingle system that includes underlayment, drip-edge flashing, rotten fascia and sheathing repairs, and full gutter and downspout replacement. The existing metal system is not suited for the damp coastal environment and has resulted in deteriorated underlayment and recurring water intrusion at the ridges. Both projects will eliminate ongoing patch repairs, resolve code-compliance issues, and protect critical infrastructure housed within each facility. Work will be coordinated with the park’s project manager but performed primarily by the roofing contractor. REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

SAINT LUCIA

UNLEASHING THE BLUE ECONOMY IN THE CARIBBEAN (UBEC)

IDA Credit # P171833

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services - Upgrade of the Leachate

 System

 

Reference No. LC-MOFED-541022-CS-CQS-ULS-26

 

Saint Lucia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) and intends to apply part of the proceeds to hiring a consulting firm to conduct a technical assessment and upgrade plan for the Deglos Leachate

 System.

 

The overall objective of this consultancy is to undertake the following tasks:

 

  • Technical Assessment of Existing Infrastructure
  • Environmental Compliance and Risk Evaluation
  • Assessment of the Operational Efficiency and Sus

System.

 

The overall objective of this consultancy is to undertake the following tasks:

 

  • Technical Assessment of Existing Infrastructure
  • Environmental Compliance and Risk Evaluation
  • Assessment of the Operational Efficiency and Sustainability of the Existing System
  • Upgrade Planning and Design
  • Prioritization and Implementation Roadmap
  • Decision-Support for Strategic Management

 

The engagement is expected to be completed within five (5) months, inclusive of the submission of deliverables to the client.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.finance.gov.lc

 

The Department of Finance now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

Firms wishing to signify their interest in undertaking the prescribed services are to submit an Expression of Interest providing information demonstrating that they have the required qualific

est in undertaking the prescribed services are to submit an Expression of Interest providing information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services.  The information submitted should follow the layout indicated below:

 

1.         Background Information including Articles of Incorporation

2.         Information on the Firm’s qualifications, experience and competence relevant to the assignment (description of similar assignments undertaken including dates undertaken and reference information of clients).

 

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations: World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers November 2020 (“Guidelines”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank’s   Procurement Regulations: World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers November 2020

Description of Work: This Presolicitation notice announces an upcoming requirement for two cedar shingle roof replacements at the Gold Beach Ranger Station, located within the Gold Beach Ranger District in Curry County, Oregon. The existing cedar shingle roofs will be removed and replaced with new cedar shingles. The Gold Beach Ranger Station, located at 29279 Ellensburg Avenue in Gold Beach, Oregon, is situated along Highway 101 within one mile of the Pacific Ocean. The site and its buildings are considered to possess historical significance. The forthcoming solicitation will detail the selection process and outline all evaluation criteria that interested offerors will be required to address. One Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) contract is anticipated to be awarded. The estimated period of performance is 90 days from issuance of the Notice to Proceed, with work expected to begin in September 2026.
